material_definitions: The class of argyrodites Li6PS5X (X = Cl, Br, I) has attracted considerable interest.
If iodine is the halide in the structure, no site-disorder occurs due to the large size mismatch between S2– and I–.
Kraft et al. found that the absence of disorder in iodine containing argyrodites is associated with high activation barriers and low ionic conductivity.

material_definitions: The effect of Ge4+ substitution in Li6+xP1-xGexS5I (argyrodite structure) was investigated to tailor structure-transport relationships.
Increasing Ge-fraction induces site disorder between the S2– and I– positions and expands the diffusion pathways for Li+.
This structural change correlates to a sharp decrease in the activation barrier and an increase in conductivity.
This approach achieved the highest lithium argyrodites reported so far, with values reaching 18.4 mS cm-1 upon sintering.

material_definitions:
A systematic study of Li(1+x)M(x)Ti(2-x)(PO4)3 with M=Al, Cr and Fe and 0 
 x 
 1 has been carried out.
The materials were characterized by X-ray and neutron powder diffraction and by impedance spectroscopy.
Lithium atoms were found to occupy two different positions, the well-known M1 and a new position called M2'.
The addition of trivalent metals gives rise to the liberation of the M1 sites and simultaneous occupation of the M2' sites, leading to higher delocalization of lithium atoms.
warnings: Raw temperature value of 25 C is an inference of 'room temperature'.

material_definitions: The studied materials are solid solutions of the type Li1+xMxTi2−x(PO4)3, where M represents Al, Fe, or Cr, substituting for Ti.
Specific compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 which showed the maximum conductivity.
The samples generally exhibit low density, ranging from 45% (LTP) to 70% (LATP03) of the theoretical density.
The charge dynamics were investigated using complex impedance measurements.

material_definitions: The solid electrolytes Li(1+x)Ti2SixP(3-x)O12 are based on the LiTi2(PO4)3 structure.
The sintering of the samples was conducted at 1473 K for 2h.
The Si4+ substitution for P5+ greatly enhances conductivity and reduces porosity.
The maximum conductivity was obtained at x = 0.3.
The Li(1+x)MxTi(2-x)(PO4)3 systems are solid solutions where Ti4+ is partially substituted by trivalent ions (M3+).
M=Al is part of the single-phase systems where M3+ replaces Ti4+ sites.
The sample was likely sintered at 1473 K based on general preparation methods for this series.
This composition (x=0.3, M=Al) showed the maximum conductivity for M3+ substitution systems.
The core material is LiTi2(PO4)3, which initially had poor ionic conductivity and high porosity in sintered pellets.
The partial substitution of the P5+ site with Si4+ or of the Ti4+ site with M3+ in the LiTi2(PO4)3 system was very effective for the enhancement of the conductivity.
The conductivity enhancement resulted mainly from the densification of the sintered pellets and the increase of the lithium content at the grain boundaries.
Mixing binders such as Li2O or Li4P2O7 with LiTi2(PO4)3 is also successful in obtaining high conductivity.
